task.description: Gate REQ-186's implementation against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md's INV-1..INV-8. Particular focus: (1) tenant isolation of the Poller's per-tenant-schema iteration -- confirm each tenant's poll/claim/fire query is genuinely scoped via that tenant's own schema prefix, with no possibility of one tenant's timer being fired/read/written under another tenant's context; (2) the DLQ-landing path (Letflow.Dlq.enqueue/2 call at max fire retries) -- confirm it lands in the SAME tenant's dlq_entries, not a global/wrong-tenant table; (3) the migration's CHECK constraints and partial index are correctly tenant-scoped per decision 0003 Decision B (if prefix() do guard); (4) no raw/interpolated SQL in the claim query (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) -- confirm it's built via Ecto.Query, not string concatenation; (5) crash isolation -- confirm a raising fire attempt in one tenant's poll cycle cannot crash or block another tenant's processing (read the Poller's per-tenant iteration and per-timer transaction boundaries).
acceptance_criteria: the timers table lives inside each tenant's Postgres schema with a tenant_id column retained (decision 0003 Decision B), verified by inspecting the migration, and carries a partial index on (fire_at) WHERE status = 'pending'
the status CHECK constraint admits exactly pending, fired, cancelled and failed -- a test attempting to insert a timer with status 'expired' fails at the database level, not only in the changeset

the recurrence CHECK constraint is all-or-nothing: a test inserting repeat_expression without repeat_interval_us is rejected by the database, and a test inserting all four recurrence columns consistently succeeds

a timer created with fire_at in the past is fired by the first poll after it exists, and the appended event carries fired_late: true together with both the scheduled fire_at and the actual firing timestamp; a timer created with fire_at in the future is NOT fired by that same poll -- two explicit tests
polling twice over the same due timer fires it exactly once: the second poll appends no second event and the timers row remains status 'fired' with its original fired_at

a fire attempt that raises increments fire_error_count and leaves the timer 'pending', AND the remaining due timers in that same poll cycle are still attempted -- one test asserts both, by making the first of two due timers fail and asserting the second still fired

a timer reaching the configured max fire retries transitions to 'failed' with failed_at set and produces exactly one dlq_entries row with entry_type "timer", and is not attempted again by subsequent polls

the poll interval, jitter, max timers per cycle and max fire retries are all read from application config with the documented defaults (5000 ms, 0 ms, 64, 3), demonstrated by a test overriding at least the interval and asserting the poller uses the override
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary:
SECURITY-REVIEWER gate on REQ-186 (timers schema and scheduler core) -- PASS. Independently read lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler/timer.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex, priv/repo/migrations/20260829020001_create_timers.exs, the application.ex/tenant_provisioning.ex diffs, and both design docs (req185-scheduler-firing-architecture.md, req186-scheduler-core.md) in full -- did not trust the implementation's own comments or moduledoc claims alone. Full findings recorded in handoffs/WF02-REQ186-20260829/security-review-req186.md.

Scope test: applies -- new migration touching a new tenant-scoped business table, a Poller/Scheduler context reading/writing tenant data across every provisioned tenant schema, and a DLQ-landing write path.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation): APPLIES, PASS. Every query in Letflow.Scheduler (claim_due_timer_ids/2, fetch_and_lock_timer/2, the fire-transaction's Repo.update, record_fire_failure/2's Repo.update) threads prefix: tenant_schema explicitly -- verified by reading each call site, not the moduledoc's claim. Letflow.Scheduler.Poller.handle_info/2 iterates Registration rows filtered on non-nil migrations_applied_at and passes each schema_name straight through to poll_and_fire/1 with no cross-iteration state. Migration's if prefix() do guard wraps the entire create table/constraints/index. tenant_id is derived server-side via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) in build_arm_changeset/2 -- arm_attrs()'s own @type has no :tenant_id key and the Map.take/2 allowlist excludes it, so a caller-supplied value is structurally impossible to smuggle in. timers is registered in @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest.

DLQ-landing: PASS. land_exhausted_timer/3 calls Dlq.enqueue(dlq_attrs, prefix: tenant_schema) with the same tenant_schema value threaded through the whole attempt_fire/2 -> record_fire_failure/2 -> land_exhausted_timer/3 call chain, inside the same Repo.transaction/1 as the fail_changeset update -- no cross-tenant DLQ write is possible.

Migration tenant-scoping (Decision 0003 Decision B): PASS. chk_timers_status and chk_timers_recurrence_shape both correctly scoped inside if prefix() do, built via Ecto.Migration's constraint/3 builder (not raw execute/1 as the design doc anticipated -- a benign, more idiomatic deviation, not a defect) matching the more recent promotion_assertion_runs precedent. Partial index idx_timers_pending_fire_at present and prefix-scoped.

No raw/interpolated SQL (INV-7): APPLIES, PASS. grep -rn Repo.query across the new files: zero hits. The FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim query is built entirely via Ecto.Query composition (where/order_by/limit/select/lock), lock/2's argument is a literal string, never interpolated with tenant/user data.

Crash isolation (INV-8): APPLIES, PASS. Verified the actual try/rescue boundaries, not the design's claim: fire_timer/2 runs inside Repo.transaction/1; attempt_fire/2 wraps the call to fire_timer/2 in an explicit try/rescue converting any escaping raise to {:error, {:raised, exception}}; any {:error, _} routes to safe_record_fire_failure/2, itself wrapped in its own rescue clause guarding record_fire_failure/2 (including Dlq.enqueue/2 itself raising). poll_and_fire/1 uses Enum.reduce/3 over the claimed id list with no short-circuit, and Poller.handle_info/2 uses a plain Enum.each/2 over tenant schemas calling poll_and_fire/1, which is verified never to raise. A raising fire attempt for one tenant/timer is trapped at two independent layers before it could reach either the per-tenant loop or the per-tick tenant-schema loop.

No data leakage: PASS. poll_and_fire/1 returns only a counts map, never row contents; TIMER_FIRED event payload and DLQ error_detail are both built solely from the one timer row already locked under that same tenant's own transaction/prefix. No route or controller file touched.

INV-2/INV-3/INV-5: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response-shaping or lookup-by-ID endpoint in this diff (S4/S5 not reached). INV-6: satisfied by this handoff's own existence.

One non-blocking flag for REVIEWER (not a security defect): Letflow.Scheduler substitutes EventStore.platform_actor_id() for the design doc's literal actor_id: nil, because EventStore.append/2's fetch_uuid/3 helper rejects nil (verified directly against event_store.ex line 222) -- confirmed accurate, not a security concern, but ELIXIR-DEV explicitly flagged it for review so REVIEWER should decide whether the design doc itself needs a one-line correction.

Verdict: PASS. No BLOCKER on any applicable invariant. Routing to REVIEWER.
